methods.signature: (params: { port: MessagePort; }) => Promise<HubRealm | undefined>
methods.summary: Join the hub through a port a page made with `createHubPort` (a document that cannot reach the hub's script): a client only, whose liveness is that page's. A port nobody answers fails the join `STORE_CONNECTION_FAILED` once the welcome budget has passed. A document that connected already gets its connection - `undefined` when that one found no hub. One the hub dropped with its page (its calls refused `STORE_ENGINE_LOST`, `realm-dropped`) joins again on the new port, on its own: the page makes it one from `onRejoined`, and a join that fails leaves it dropped until the next one.

methods.signature: (params?: ConnectHubParams) => Promise<HubRealm | undefined>
methods.summary: Connect this page to the origin's hub, once: a second call - from this copy of the library or another one of the same protocol - gets the same connection. Answers `undefined` where the browser has no SharedWorker, or the hub never welcomed the page (its script failed to load or was blocked, or it stayed silent): a later call tries again. A hub of another protocol refuses the page: `STORE_PROTOCOL_MISMATCH`; the browser refusing to make the hub's worker (a `DOMException`) is no hub, any other error thrown making it is thrown. The page registers the engines it can start whose worker is of its own origin (each dialecte's `factory.spawner`); a later call adds those it does not run yet - a project opened on `sqlite` adds its own as it opens - and one naming a dialecte the page runs at another version is refused `STORE_HUB_SPAWNERS_FIXED`, the connection kept. A document that joined through `adoptHubPort` hosts no engine: the spawners it names are not registered; neither are those of a page that cannot store (no private file system; two versions of one dialecte refused all the same): its own projects on `sqlite` are refused `STORE_UNAVAILABLE` unless its page bound it, its connection serving to hand ports to its children. An engine's files (the SQLite wasm) are fetched when the page first starts one.
